# Model card: Standard (no privacy)

*Generated 2026-11-24 17:46 UTC from the FairDP demo backend.*

## Model details
- Architecture: MLP 64 → 32 → 1, trained 10 epochs, seed 0
- Training method: `erm`; no privacy guarantee
- Code version: 03644ca (uncommitted changes); torch 2.15.0+cpu, opacus 1.6.0

## Intended use
- Research and teaching demonstration of privacy–fairness trade-offs.
- Task: predict whether income exceeds $50k (UCI Adult). Decisions at threshold 0.5.
- Not for real lending, hiring or benefit decisions. Credit scoring is a high-risk use under the EU AI Act (Annex III) and would need a full conformity assessment.

## Data
- Dataset `adult`: 48,790 rows (fingerprint `4fcf5cd61755f842`), split 34,153 / 4,879 / 9,758 (train / val / test).
- Sensitive attributes: sex, race, age; 18 intersectional groups in the test set.

## Performance (test set)
| Accuracy | Balanced accuracy | Recall | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|
| 85.5% | 78.4% | 64.9% | 91.4% |

## Fairness
| Attribute | Disparate-impact ratio | Four-fifths rule | Equal-opportunity diff | Equalized-odds diff | Calibration gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sex | 0.305 | fail | 9.9% | 9.9% | 1.5% |
| race | 0.438 | fail | 7.1% | 7.1% | 2.5% |
| age | 0.147 | fail | 22.6% | 22.6% | 2.2% |
| intersection | 0.066 | fail | 33.1% | 33.1% | 8.4% |

- Worst intersectional-group recall: 44.2%; individual consistency (kNN): 0.899

## Privacy evaluation
- Loss-threshold membership-inference AUC: 0.498 (0.5 = chance).

## Limitations and ethical considerations
- The privacy guarantee covers model training only; preprocessing statistics (scaler, encoder) and the list of group categories are not privatised.
- Groups with fewer than 30 people or 10 positives are excluded from gap metrics; their estimates are unreliable.
- Group gaps describe outcomes and do not by themselves prove causal discrimination; race and sex categories in census data are coarse.
- Results come from one training seed; see the multi-seed study for variability. Significance claims need ≥ 10 seeds (5-seed Wilcoxon tests cannot reach p < 0.05).
- Method settings were chosen on a pilot run of the same dataset; that selection is not covered by the privacy guarantee.
- Group categories (the cell schema) are treated as public information; IG-DPSGD sees roughly batch-size / #cells people per cell per step, so its noisy group statistics are dominated by noise for small cells.
- Post-processed (group-threshold) results use non-private validation data and are not covered by the same ε.

- Sensitive attributes: sex, race, age; 18 intersectional groups in the test set.

## Performance (test set)
| Accuracy | Balanced accuracy | Recall | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|
| 84.1% | 80.0% | 72.1% | 90.5% |

## Fairness
| Attribute | Disparate-impact ratio | Four-fifths rule | Equal-opportunity diff | Equalized-odds diff | Calibration gap |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| sex | 0.469 | fail | 3.3% | 7.2% | 2.7% |
| race | 0.543 | fail | 9.5% | 9.5% | 5.8% |
| age | 0.248 | fail | 7.3% | 14.0% | 0.8% |
| intersection | 0.154 | fail | 21.9% | 21.9% | 12.8% |

- Worst intersectional-group recall: 58.9%; individual consistency (kNN): 0.901

## Privacy evaluation
- Loss-threshold membership-inference AUC: 0.496 (0.5 = chance).

## Limitations and ethical considerations
- The privacy guarantee covers model training only; preprocessing statistics (scaler, encoder) and the list of group categories are not privatised.
- Groups with fewer than 30 people or 10 positives are excluded from gap metrics; their estimates are unreliable.
- Group gaps describe outcomes and do not by themselves prove causal discrimination; race and sex categories in census data are coarse.
- Results come from one training seed; see the multi-seed study for variability. Significance claims need ≥ 10 seeds (5-seed Wilcoxon tests cannot reach p < 0.05).
- Method settings were chosen on a pilot run of the same dataset; that selection is not covered by the privacy guarantee.
- Group categories (the cell schema) are treated as public information; IG-DPSGD sees roughly batch-size / #cells people per cell per step, so its noisy group statistics are dominated by noise for small cells.
- Post-processed (group-threshold) results use non-private validation data and are not covered by the same ε.
